scope: silver-bearing material identification, mechanical segregation, testing, and refinery routing

workflow.title: Identify source
workflow.instruction: Record whether the suspected silver-bearing material came from contacts, relays, switchgear, plated hardware, jewelry/tableware, or another source.

workflow.title: Do not grade by color
workflow.instruction: Treat silver-colored material as unknown until markings, source knowledge, non-destructive testing, or professional assay supports an identification.

workflow.title: Preserve markings
workflow.instruction: Photograph hallmarks, alloy stamps, part numbers, and source assemblies before separating material.

workflow.title: Mechanically segregate
workflow.instruction: When justified, separate suspected silver-bearing pieces from copper, brass, steel, plastic, and other fractions without burning or creating unknown-metal dust.

workflow.title: Keep lots by source
workflow.instruction: Do not mix unlike contact alloys or plated material with known sterling or other identified silver grades.

workflow.title: Test or route for assay
workflow.instruction: Use appropriate non-destructive/professional testing or refinery assay when composition materially affects value.

workflow.title: Compare sale/refinery value
workflow.instruction: Use weight, confirmed grade when available, Scrap Radar silver reference price, and buyer/refinery terms to compare options.

hazard_policy: Chemical stripping/refining and thermal processing are controlled operations with corrosive, toxic, and waste-handling hazards. This lab provides sorting, testing, value, and professional refinery-routing guidance rather than hazardous recipes.
